findings.claim: The round-4 merge fix's sort -un destroys the root-first file invariant that kill_recorded_tree relies on, so the post-hang teardown can walk and re-walk from the wrong root.
findings.evidence: kill_recorded_tree parses the pid file positionally (sed -n 1p) and every other writer keeps the driver root on line 1; the sort -un merge makes line 1 the lowest PID instead. TERM/KILL of the recorded list itself is unaffected because all merged PIDs remain in the recorded set.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve root-first ordering in the merged file, or pass the root PID as a second argument to kill_recorded_tree.

findings.claim: The per-tick snapshot refresh replaces rather than accumulates the recorded list, so a PID that reparents mid-run is silently dropped one tick later and is unreachable by teardown.
findings.evidence: The per-tick writer overwrites last.pid with only the currently-walkable set; the function's own header comment promises the recorded list reaches reparented children. Pre-existing since round 2; the never-replace principle was applied only to the post-capture refresh.
findings.suggested_fix: Accumulate per tick (merge previous file + current walk), keeping the root-first convention.

findings.claim: The caveats note documents only clean-perturbed as the post-hang label, omitting failed-perturbed from the round-4 label vocabulary.
findings.evidence: The script emits failed/failed-perturbed as well as clean/clean-perturbed; the evidence-pack note defines only the latter.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the note to name both post-hang labels.
